title: fix(core): refuse the two $icontains comparand shapes FILTER_TEXT_CASES declares refused (objectui#9001)
body:
Fixes #9001

`@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` carries an empty `$icontains` comparand and a non-string one as REJECTION rows, each with `code: 'INVALID_FILTER'` and `mustMention: ['$icontains']`. `ValueDataSource` has answered both since objectui#8748 (`refuseTextComparand`); `convertFiltersToAST` answered neither, so one authored filter had two fates decided by which data source was behind the view.

Triage's ruling was **port, do not re-design** — there is a shipped, reviewed reference implementation one data source over. This is that port.

## Measured, on today's `origin/main`

Base `152f0a700`, with both of today's movers on this file already landed (objectui#8996 added `$icontains` to `operatorMap` as an identity, objectui#9019 folded the TRUE identity at the tail). Every anchor was re-derived; nothing is quoted from the card body. Spec `17.4.0`, both faces in one process:

```
BEFORE
$icontains ''    LOWER=["name","icontains",""]     MATCH=[] REFUSED(1)
$icontains 42    LOWER=["name","icontains",42]     MATCH=[] REFUSED(1)
$icontains null  LOWER=["name","icontains",null]   MATCH=[] REFUSED(1)
$icontains 'acme' LOWER=["name","icontains","acme"] MATCH=["a","b"] REFUSED(0)

AFTER
$icontains ''    THROWS FilterOperatorError  code=INVALID_FILTER  httpStatus=400
$icontains 42    THROWS FilterOperatorError  code=INVALID_FILTER  httpStatus=400
$icontains 'acme' LOWER=["name","icontains","acme"]  (unchanged, byte for byte)
```

`REFUSED(n)` counts the matcher's drained `console.warn` refusals.

## What transfers from the sibling, and what does not

The **discrimination** (`typeof target !== 'string' || target === ''`) and the **message** are the sibling's, verbatim. The message is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: `mustMention: ['$icontains']` means a differently-worded refusal is a *different* failure to honour the same row, so the test drives BOTH faces, strips `ValueDataSource`'s envelope, and asserts this converter's message CONTAINS the matcher's refusal reason. Neither face can drift without that reddening.

The **delivery** deliberately does not transfer, and that is the card's own Q1 answered by the two call sites rather than by a fresh ruling. `ValueDataSource` excludes-and-logs because it is deciding about one ROW and has a row to exclude; `convertFiltersToAST` is the producer deciding whether to send a query at all and has none. Its declared refusal shape is `FilterOperatorError`, which carries exactly the `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 envelope the spec rows declare and which this file already uses for `$regex`, `$not`, the retired aliases and three other comparand shapes. Same code, same words, each face's own envelope — pinned by a case asserting the two envelopes DIFFER, so "port the message" cannot be misread as "port the delivery".

`ValueDataSource` is **not edited by this PR**. Three cases pin that it still answers what objectui#8748 made it answer.

## Verification

Package-scale runs went through `../objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; the verdict line quoted for the typecheck+lint pair was `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` are CI's runs, declared rather than taken locally.

## Ablation — prediction written first, then measured

Removing ONLY the five-line guard call site (the helper and its docblock left in place, so the compile still succeeds and the ablation cannot pass for the trivial reason).

**Predicted red: 7 of 16.** The two contract rows driven through the converter, the "nothing lowers" case, the two mirror cases, the differing-envelopes case, and the BigInt-envelope case. **Predicted green: 9** — the three controls, the three `ValueDataSource`-is-unchanged cases, and the three "must NOT touch" cases (valid lowering, sibling operators, TRUE-identity tail).

**Measured: `Tests 7 failed | 9 passed (16)`** — the same seven, one for one. The lead diagnostic reads `convertFiltersToAST({"name":{"$icontains":""}}) did NOT refuse — it lowered ["name","icontains",""] onto the wire. That is objectui#9001.`

On-disk proof rather than an editor exit code: the target's blob hash moved `14dc2eac…` → `52137451…` under mutation, the removed anchor counted `1 → 0` and the injected marker `0 → 1`; after a `git checkout HEAD --` of that one PATH (spelled as a word here because GitHub's body sanitizer eats angle-bracket-shaped placeholders) the blob returned to `14dc2eac…` (equal to the `HEAD` blob), `git diff HEAD` was empty, and both counts returned. The script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restoring by absolute path.

**One difference from the prediction, reported rather than tidied away.** The BigInt case reddened in the right direction but through `JSON.stringify`'s own "Do not know how to serialize a BigInt" inside the test's *diagnostic*, so its failure text named the harness instead of the defect. Fixed in the second commit (the diagnostic is now total) and the ablation re-run: same 7/9, and that case now names the defect.

## The dispatching seat's mechanism assumptions, falsified or confirmed

- **(a) `refuseTextComparand` transfers.** *Partly — and the half that does not is the interesting half.* Its discrimination and message transfer verbatim; its delivery cannot, because it takes a `refusals` Set and returns `false` to exclude a row, and this face has no row. See above. This is the shape the port takes, not an obstacle to it.
- **(b) `convertFiltersToAST` is a published export.** *Confirmed.* `packages/core/src/index.ts:23` is `export * from './utils/filter-converter.js';` — measured on this base, not quoted.
- **(c) The file moved twice today.** *Confirmed and re-derived.* `$icontains` is in `operatorMap` as an identity (`convertOperatorToAST('$icontains') === 'icontains'`, pinned in the new suite) and the TRUE-identity fold is at the tail. Everything above was measured on `152f0a700`.
- **(d) The guard belongs where the comparand is read.** *Confirmed, and the card's guess would have missed.* Because `$icontains` is an identity, the comparand is read at the single generic push `conditions.push([field, astOperator, operatorValue])` — there is no `$icontains`-specific lowering arm to hang a guard on. The guard sits immediately before that push, keyed on the LOWERED operator (the rule belongs to `icontains` itself, and `ValueDataSource`'s AST arm is keyed the same way) while the `$` spelling the author wrote travels into the message, which is what `mustMention` is about.
- **(e) Interaction with objectui#9030.** *Measured: none.* That finding is about the tail's `trueIdentityGroups === Object.keys(filter).length` comparison counting keys the loop `continue`s past. The new path **throws**; it adds no `continue`, skips no key, and the tail is unreachable from it. Pinned by a case asserting `{ $and: [] }`, `{ $or: [{}] }`, `{ $and: [], a: null }`, `{}`, `{ a: null }` and `{ $and: [], name: { $icontains: 'x' } }` all answer exactly what they answered before. objectui#9030 is **not** touched here.

Also re-derived at the moment of writing rather than taken from the dispatch snapshot: no open PR touches `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`. objectui#9037 is the only other open PR in `packages/core`, and its files (`src/index.ts`, `src/utils/object-aggregate-query.ts`) do not overlap this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- **Scope boundary, deliberate.** `$contains` / `$startsWith` / `$endsWith` are untouched — the table declares no such row for them, and widening by analogy is the published table's decision, not this converter's. That asymmetry is pinned so the next reader sees a boundary rather than an oversight, the same line `refuseTextComparand`'s own docblock draws.
- **Out of scope, filed:** objectui#9048 — after this PR the same wire node is still lowered by the two OBJECT-FORM producer paths, `viewFilterRuleToNode` (stored view rules, same file) and `objectFilterEntryToAST` (`@object-ui/data-objectstack`'s entry-form array branch). Measured. Not folded in: the stored-view blast radius is a render-time throw on metadata an absent author saved, the `mustMention` spelling cannot be ported into a vocabulary with no `$`, and the second half crosses a package. objectui#9001's own body had already recorded the `data-objectstack` entrance as pre-existing; the `viewFilterRuleToNode` sibling was not previously named anywhere.
- **Noted, not filed:** `@object-ui/data-objectstack`'s `translateFilterToAST` object branch delegates to this function, so its `$`-dialect route inherits the refusal with no source change of its own — recorded in the changeset rather than as a card, because it is this PR's own consequence and the carrier is this PR.
- **Clause-② is `yes`** on the card (comment 5624872568): a published export's observable answer changes for input it accepts today, in the narrowing direction. `needs:contract-review` is deliberately **not** touched by this seat — that claim comment explains why, and this PR does not alter that disposition in either direction.
- Draft, and **not** enabled for auto-merge: landing is the dispatching seat's.

Session reference for this run: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`

## Rework after the first CI round — one red shard, genuinely mine

`Test (shard 4/4)` failed on `packages/data-objectstack/src/readme-filter-operator-table.test.ts` (the objectui#8558 pin), reporting `packages/data-objectstack/README.md:160: $icontains is refused by convertFiltersToAST, so it is not a supported operator`. Reproduced locally before changing anything, then read the harness rather than guessing at it.

**What the harness actually did.** `lowerings(spelling)` asked the converter what each README spelling lowers to by probing it with the two BOOLEANS, `[true, false]`, and treated the FIRST refusal as "this operator is refused". Its own docblock stated the premise: the two booleans exist because `$null` / `$exists` read their value to pick a direction, and *"for every other operator the value is irrelevant and both probes agree"*. This PR ended that premise — `$icontains` now has a comparand door, so a boolean probe measures the COMPARAND and answers a refusal. A supported operator was reported as unsupported by an instrument asking the wrong question. Neither the page nor the converter was wrong.

**What changed.** The probe set gains a string (`PROBE_COMPARANDS = [true, false, 'probe']`) and `refused` now means *refused for EVERY comparand* rather than *refused for the first one tried*; the emitted operators are the union over the probes that lower. Per the coordinator's fence 4, this is the per-operator-valid-comparand repair done as a general rule rather than as an `$icontains` special case, and it makes the pin stronger than it was found: it now distinguishes "this operator is not supported" from "this operator constrains its comparand", which it previously could not, and the `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 envelope assertion now runs on EVERY refusing probe instead of only the first — so a comparand door that refuses outside the envelope is caught here too.

**The pin is not weakened, and that is measured, not asserted.** Two ablations, each with on-disk proof and a verified restore:

- *A wrong operator in the table must still fail.* Changing the README's `$nin` row to name `notin` reddens with the objectui#8558 message it was written for: `README.md:154: $nin lowers to nin, the row says notin`.
- *A genuinely refused operator must still be reported refused.* Making the converter refuse `$icontains` for EVERY comparand reddens with the original message, `README.md:160: $icontains is refused by convertFiltersToAST, so it is not a supported operator` — three cases red, including the new control.

Both README and converter blobs returned to their `HEAD` hashes with an empty `git diff HEAD` and no markers left behind.

**A control keeps the third probe honest.** `the string probe is load-bearing, and this is the operator that proves it` asserts both halves: a boolean `$icontains` comparand must still be refused (if it stops being, the string probe may go) and a valid one must still lower (if it stops, the rescue does not work and the repair is elsewhere). Without it the third probe is an unexplained entry the next reader tidies away, and CI goes red again on a page and a converter that are both correct.

**The README gains one paragraph, and its `$icontains` row is untouched.** `$icontains` **is** still a supported operator — this PR constrains its comparand, not its support — so the row stays exactly as it was and the new paragraph sits beside the existing `$null` / `$exists` note, saying that this one operator constrains its comparand and what to write instead. No row was added to the "Refused at lowering time" table: that would have been false, and it would have reddened the refused-table pin, which requires those spellings to be refused for every comparand.

The `Build Docs` surface was checked rather than assumed: `content/docs/guide/data-source.md` links to this README by heading anchor, no heading moved, and `docs:check-links` reports `Links are valid across 17 scan roots`.

**On the narrowing, declared rather than hidden.** The full dependents closure of `@object-ui/core` is 38 packages — effectively the whole repo, and one shard alone took 18 minutes on this shared box. Rather than claim a run I did not make, the breadth above is: one full quarter of the repo (shard 1/4), the two directly-affected packages in full, the five packages owning every remaining source that mentions `icontains`, and every remaining test file that mentions it. That last population is exhaustive for this change — the new guard fires only when the lowered operator is `icontains`, so a file that never names it cannot reach the new throw. The population was read with `git grep -l -i icontains` and both controls fired (1472 files for a token that must be everywhere, 0 for a token that must be nowhere). The remaining three shards are CI's.

`needs:contract-review` remains untouched in either direction.
